red_green_evidence: Root cause confirmed structurally first: FormDesigner.jsx's `{registryDefs && (...)}` picker block (the exact block that crashed in T-0706, 'Cannot read properties of null (reading map)') lives inside `{!initialFields && (...)}` (line 1276) — it ONLY renders when the `initialFields` prop is ABSENT. Every existing FormDesigner.test.jsx render() call passes `initialFields={FIELDS}` (documented 'embedding/test mode'), so the crashing block was structurally UNREACHABLE by any pre-existing test, static or otherwise — confirming the file's own documented 'MOUNT-GAP'. RED experiment: reintroduced the pre-fix line verbatim (`{registryDefs && (` -> `{registryDefs && boundRegistryDef ? (`, i.e. dropped the outer null-guard so the ternary's last arm calls `registryDefs.map` unconditionally when registryDefs===null). Ran the FULL web suite under the break: 2 of 2829 tests failed (2 new tests existed at that point, only FormDesigner.mount.test.jsx). Of the 2827 PRE-EXISTING tests, only ONE failed — a string-literal 'regression lock' pin in FormDesigner.test.jsx that was added specifically after the T-0706 incident to grep for this exact source pattern (brittle: matches literal text, not behavior). The other 2826 pre-existing tests, including all 47 other assertions in FormDesigner's own sibling test file (render-smoke, fullscreen invariant, T-0665/T-0669/T-0706/T-0711/T-0682 wiring, etc.), stayed GREEN while the real /forms screen would white-screen on mount. The NEW FormDesigner.mount.test.jsx failed for the RIGHT reason: an actual uncaught React render exception, `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'map')` thrown from FormDesigner.jsx:1348 during renderWithHooks -- i.e. it reproduced T-0706 live, via real behavior, not a source grep. Reverted the break (git diff on FormDesigner.jsx came back empty -- byte-identical to before); both FormDesigner.test.jsx (48/48) and FormDesigner.mount.test.jsx (2/2) went back GREEN. Secondary organic evidence (screen-inbox): while authoring InboxScreen's mount test with a plausible generic task fixture, the REAL component crashed (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'left')` in SLACell, screen-inbox.jsx:480) because the fixture omitted the `sla` field that SLACell reads with no fallback -- confirming, independently and without any deliberate source edit, that a real mount test surfaces exactly this class of gap (a required-but-unguarded field) that a source-presence test cannot see at all. Fixed the fixture to carry a realistic `sla` object (matching the real API contract) and the test went GREEN; this is now a live regression net for SLACell.

environment_investigation.why_no_jsdom_before: web/vitest.config.js was deliberately 'node' env (per its own header comment, T-0408): all .jsx screen tests were written as source-presence assertions against the raw .jsx text, or as renderToStaticMarkup single-pass renders (no effects/no re-renders) specifically BECAUSE neither jsdom nor @testing-library/react was ever a dependency anywhere in the repo (root or web node_modules/package.json) -- confirmed by direct search before starting this task. This is exactly the D-064 gap: 'mirror'/source-presence conventions were adopted as a workaround for a missing capability, not a deliberate choice, and several existing test files (FormDesigner.test.jsx's own P0 describe block, screen-inbox.test.jsx's InboxTaskForm comments) already self-documented the resulting 'MOUNT-GAP' in their own doc comments.
environment_investigation.fix: Installed @testing-library/react@^16.3.2 and jsdom@^29.1.1 as web devDependencies (web/package.json + package-lock.json). No global vitest.config.js split was needed: vitest 3.2.6 (the version already resolved from web/node_modules) supports a per-file `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock pragma (verified against node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.*.js's `/@(?:vitest|jest)-environment\s+([\w-]+)\b/` matcher) -- each new *.mount.test.jsx file opts into jsdom individually; all pre-existing test files keep running in the fast 'node' env, unaffected.
environment_investigation.node_modules_caveat: web/node_modules (and root node_modules) are symlinks to /Users/shoxy/Code/choros/node_modules (the trunk checkout) -- this worktree's node_modules is NOT private. `npm install` therefore wrote the new packages into the SHARED trunk node_modules (consistent with this repo's established 'npm install after merge' convention, DURABLE note from prior runs). web/package.json and web/package-lock.json themselves are real files in THIS worktree and are committed normally.
